description: Controlled vocabulary of occupations from MarineLives Semantic MediaWiki (category 'Semantic occupation'). 149 occupation types (plus Form:SemOccupation listed in wiki as a form, not an occupation). Used to normalise occupation names extracted from HCA deposition front matter.

version_history.context: Initial creation from MarineLives data, but file in skill folder and Customize was truncated at 5,346 bytes mid-context_dependent dict.

Reconstructed from authoritative MarineLives source (https://www.marinelives.org/wiki/Category:Semantic_occupation, 150 pages). Added entries missing from v1.0 truncation: Bosun, Corne Meter, Fisherman, Skipper. Completed context_dependent dict and added excluded_statuses (Widow). Closed JSON properly.

usage: Match the raw occupation extracted from front matter against entries in each category (case-insensitive). Strip Unicode accent marks (NFD normalisation) before matching — transcriptions contain marks like merćhant. Common C17th spelling variants must be handled: marriner/marryner → Mariner, marchant → Merchant, joyner → Joiner, chirurgian → Chirurgion, sailemaker/sail maker → Sailmaker, ships carpenter/ships=carpenter → Ship carpenter, brewers clerke → Brewer's clerk. When an occupation appears in context_dependent, the correct category depends on whether the deponent served aboard a vessel (seafaring/shore maritime) or on land. If no match is found after variant expansion, flag the record as UNMATCHED for human review. The excluded_statuses (Widow, Bachelor) are social statuses, not occupations — if encountered, record as a separate field, not as occupation.
notes: Statuses (Widow, Bachelor) are excluded — they are recorded as Person properties, not Occupation nodes. Some occupations are context-dependent across categories (e.g. Carpenter may be 'Wood trades' or 'Shore maritime trades' depending on whether the deponent is a ship carpenter). Bosun is a synonym for Boatswain (kept separately because the MarineLives wiki lists them separately). Skipper is a synonym for Master (same).
